questiontext.text:
A function \( f : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) (where \(\mathbb{R}\) denotes the real numbers) is defined by the rule \[ f(x) = {@f1@}. \]

What is the output of the function \(f\) when the input is \({@n1@}\)? Give your answer as a whole number or a fraction, not as a power.

\(f({@n1@}) = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
To find the output of a function for a given input, substitute the input for \(x\) in the rule. Here \(f(x) = {@f1@}\) is an exponential function: the variable \(x\) is the index (the power), and the base \({@b@}\) is fixed.

[[if test="is(n1<0)"]]

The input is negative, so use the rule for a negative index, \(a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}\). A negative index gives a reciprocal, not a negative number:

\[ f({@n1@}) = {@b@}^{ {@n1@} } = \dfrac{1}{ {@b@}^{ {@negn1@} } } = {@correctanswer@}. \]

[[else]]

A positive whole-number index means repeated multiplication of the base by itself, not multiplication by the index:

\[ f({@n1@}) = {@b@}^{ {@n1@} } = {@correctanswer@}. \]

[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions (function notation: evaluating; overlaps with 16.2 Function Notation). Evaluates an exponential function b^x at a positive or negative integer input.

node.description: Form: the power has been worked out

falsefeedback.text: Your answer has the right value, but it is not worked out. Calculate the power and enter the result as a single whole number or fraction.

node.description: Diagnostic: a negative index read as a negative number (n1 negative), or the base multiplied by the index (n1 positive)

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(n1<0)"]]

A negative index does not make the answer negative. It gives a reciprocal: \(a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}\).

[[else]]

It looks as if you multiplied the base by the input. In \({@f1@}\) the input is a power: \(a^n\) means \(a\) multiplied by itself \(n\) times, not \(a \times n\).

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Substitute the input for \(x\) in the rule \(f(x) = {@f1@}\) and work out the power. For a negative index, use \(a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}\).
